source: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023 (CCPA, notified 30 Nov 2023), Annexure 1

patterns.name: False urgency
patterns.summary: Falsely stating or implying urgency or scarcity, including fake popularity or understated stock, to push an immediate purchase or action.

patterns.name: Basket sneaking
patterns.summary: Adding products, services, donations or payments at checkout without the user’s consent so the total exceeds what they chose.

patterns.name: Confirm shaming
patterns.summary: Using words, video, audio or other means to make the user feel fear, shame, ridicule or guilt so they buy or keep subscribing.

patterns.name: Forced action
patterns.summary: Making the user buy something extra, sign up for an unrelated service, or share personal data to get the thing they came for.

patterns.name: Subscription trap
patterns.summary: Making cancellation impossible, hidden, long or confusing, or demanding payment details or auto-debit for a free subscription.

patterns.name: Interface interference
patterns.summary: Design that highlights some information and obscures other relevant information to misdirect the user from the action they want.

patterns.name: Bait and switch
patterns.summary: Advertising one outcome for the user’s action but deceptively serving a different one, typically a pricier substitute.

patterns.name: Drip pricing
patterns.summary: Hiding price elements until late, charging more than the checkout price, calling something free without disclosing paid continuation, or blocking a paid service until more is bought.

patterns.name: Disguised advertisement
patterns.summary: Ads made to look like user content, news or other non-ad content so users click on them without knowing they are ads.

patterns.name: Nagging
patterns.summary: Repeated, persistent requests or interruptions that disrupt the user to push a transaction, unless the user has specifically allowed them.

patterns.name: Trick question
patterns.summary: Deliberately confusing or vague wording, such as double negatives, that misleads the user into a response they did not intend.

patterns.name: SaaS billing
patterns.summary: Recurring billing designed to collect money as quietly as possible: silent trial conversion, unannounced renewals, charging for unused features.

patterns.name: Rogue malware
patterns.summary: Ransomware or scareware that tricks users into believing their device is infected or locks their files to extract payment.
